page: Amazon Web Services i3.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance provisioned on the Xen hypervisor, designed for I/O-intensive workloads requiring direct access to local non-volatile storage. The hardware is built on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 244.0 GB, yielding 7.62 GB per physical core. For high-throughput local operations, the server integrates 7600 GB of NVMe SSD storage. The network baseline throughput is rated at 12 Gbps, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance registers in the lower tiers, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 857.4 and a Geekbench single-core score of 892.0, both categorized in the bottom 10%. Text processing via Geekbench (1154.0) and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (7.06 GB/sec) also place in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-threaded aggregate performance scales into the middle 50% across most suites, with a stress-ng multi-core result of 16172.46, Geekbench multi-core score of 7534.0, and PassMark CPU score of 20268.57. Memory bandwidth tests yield 1225.62 GB/sec for small cached reads and 58.35 GB/sec for uncached large reads, although large block writes drop to 24.77 GB/sec, falling into the bottom 25%.

Application-level throughput reflects the balance of abundant thread parallelism and broad NVMe capacity. Redis operations reach 20.29 million SET operations per second, PassMark database operations record 9119.26, and static web serving throughput measures 16.35 GB/sec, all matching the middle 50% benchmark segment. Natural language inference shows solid small-model prompt handling (869.79 tokens/sec) and generation (154.96 tokens/sec), but generation falls off for 7B models down to 8.73 tokens/sec in the bottom 25%. From an operational perspective, the instance provides cost efficiency primarily through its high density of bundled NVMe storage and RAM, making it suitable for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing engines, and analytical ETL pipelines that prioritize local storage throughput over cutting-edge single-threaded compute.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor at 2.3 GHz, 244.0 GB of memory, and 7600 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the Xen hypervisor, it features a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated GPUs. Performance benchmarks show below-average single-core CPU throughput, while multi-threaded benchmarks, database operations, and Redis throughput consistently perform within the median range. Uncached memory write speeds remain modest compared to read operations. Given its high local storage volume, large RAM footprint, and multi-core parallelism, the i3.8xlarge is suitable for NoSQL databases, in-memory caches, data analytics clusters, and write-heavy transactional workloads.
